Lines creation.

Line creation through two points.

Parallel line creation. Click first on a line, ray, vector or segment then on a point.

Angle bisector creation.

Perpendicular bisector creation.

Line defined through point and slope.

Line defined by an equation in a frame. The equation may be of any kind, for instance 2*x+3*y-5 = 0 or x = rac(2) or y = rac(2)*x+1

Horizontal line creation.

Vertical line creation.

Tangent creation on a curve by specifying abscissa of the point. It is the result of an internal macro-construction.

Line of linear regression of a set of points. Click on the points then click on the red button STOP.

To be noted : A matrix is created along with the line. This matrix contains the coordinates of the points clicked.

If your figure contains more than one frame, you will be asked to choose the frame (and confirm the matrix name).

Point locus, function curves, object locus and sequences graphs creation.

Creation of a linked point locus generated through a linked point.

Creation of a linked point locus generated through a variable.

Creation of a not connected point locus generated through a linked point.

Creation of a not connected point locus generated through a variable.

To create a curved segment (Bézier curve). Click on two points. A point locus appears as a segment with in the middle a control point in the form of a small cross that allows to deform the "segment".

Graph of a real function creation in a frame (on a segment or an interval).

Graph of a real function on an interval with one or two brackets at the interval edge.

Graph of a function going through n given points giving the tangent slope at these points (n ranging from 2 to 10)

If you check the checkbox Use only one polynomial function, an unique polynomial function filling the required conditions will be created and you can get the coefficients of this function in a matrix name of which starts with coef.

If you don't check the checkbox Use only one polynomial function, on each interval changing the formula, the formula of a polynomial function of degree 3 will be used.

In both cases, a function is created, it's name starting with f.

Beware : If you don't check Use only one polynomial function, the order of the x-coordinates of the clicked points must not be changed for the curve to remain accurate.

Graph of a polynomial function curve going through n points (n ranging from 2 to 8).

Creation of the graph of a real recurrent sequence kind of u(n+1)=f[u(n)].

Creation of the graph of a complex recurrent sequence kind of z(n+1)=f[z(n)]., where f is a complex function.

Creation of an object locus generated through a linked point.

Creation of an object locus generated through a variable.


Geometrical transformations.

Creation of image objects through a translation. Click first on the starting point and ending point of the translation vector. Vector of translation blinks. Then click on an object to create it's image (line; ray, segment, circle, circle arc, polygon, broken line, point locus). You can click on several objects (as long as the vector is blinking).

Creation of image objects through a axial symmetry. Click first on the symmetry axis (line, ray, segment). Axis blinks. Then click on an object to create it's image (line; ray, segment, circle, circle arc, polygon, broken line, point locus). You can click on several objects (as long as the axis is blinking).

Creation of image objects through a central symmetry. Click first on the symmetry center (point). Center blinks. Then click on an object to create it's image (line; ray, segment, circle, circle arc, polygon, broken line, point locus). You can click on several objects (as long as the center of symmetry is blinking).

Creation of image objects through a rotation. Click first on the rotation center (point). A dialog box pops up. Enter the angle of rotation. Then click on an object to create it's image (line; ray, segment, circle, circle arc, polygon, broken line, point locus). You can click on several objects (as long as the center of rotation is blinking).

Use of a virtual protractor in order to rotate a point around another one.

Creation of image objects through a translation by giving the translation vector coordinates in frame. Enter first the vector coordinates in the dialog box then click on an object to create it's image (line; ray, segment, circle, circle arc, polygon, broken line, point locus). You can click on several objects (as long as the translation vector is blinking).

Creation of image objects through a  dilation. Click first on the dilation center (point). A dialog box pops up. Enter the dilation ratio. Then click on an object to create it's image (line; ray, segment, circle, circle arc, polygon, broken line, point locus). You can click on several objects (as long as the center of dilation is blinking).

Creation of image objects through a  direct similitude. Click first on the dilation center (point). A dialog box pops up. Enter the similitude ratio and angle. Then click on an object to create it's image (line; ray, segment, circle, circle arc, polygon, broken line, point locus). You can click on several objects (as long as the center of similitude is blinking).
